summary: Adds symmetric reduce() methods so AddIndex/RemoveIndex pairs cancel during migration optimization, matching the issue intent. However the methods are inserted before each class docstring (demoting it to dead code) and the Remove-then-Add collapse can silently drop a differently-defined index sharing the same name.

issues.description: RemoveIndex.reduce() collapses RemoveIndex('foo') followed by AddIndex(Index(name='foo', ...)) to [], but RemoveIndex only stores the name, not the index definition. If the re-added 'foo' differs from the removed one (different fields/conditions), the optimizer cannot prove equivalence, so dropping both leaves the OLD index in place and loses the new definition — a behavioral regression in the optimizer.

reduce() is inserted as the first statement of each class body, ahead of the string literal `"""Add an index on a model."""` / `"""Remove an index from a model."""`. Since the string is no longer the first statement, it stops being the class docstring and becomes a no-op expression. Method should be placed after the docstring.
The single-line isinstance condition far exceeds Django's enforced line length (black/flake8, 88 cols) and would fail the project's lint/CI style checks; condition should be wrapped.
